title: Art & Architecture North
subtitle: Final Composite Draft
summary: Hand-drafted plans, sections, elevations and perspectives of the Art & Architecture Building North, brought together in a final composite.
description: This project introduced architectural drafting through the study of the Art & Architecture Building North.
The work included hand-drafted floor plans, sections, elevations and perspectives, focused on understanding the building and the relationship between two-dimensional and three-dimensional space.
concept: The final composite brings the drawings together to show the drafting process and the development of foundational skills in architectural documentation, observation and visual communication.

process.label: Research
process.note: Studying the Art & Architecture Building North through observation.

process.label: Drawing
process.note: Floor plans, sections, elevations and perspectives drafted by hand.

process.label: Final
process.note: A composite that brings the drawings together.

images.alt: Final composite draft: marker-rendered perspective of the Art & Architecture Building North over a drafted elevation

pitch: Hand-drafted plans, sections, elevations and perspectives, brought together in a single composite. It shows how a building is observed, understood and drawn, from flat plan to three-dimensional space.

title: Quiet Harbor
subtitle: Hand Renderings P1
summary: Four hand-rendered iterations of one interior, each shaped by a written narrative and a different technique.
description: This project explored how different hand-rendering techniques influence the atmosphere and perception of an interior space.
Catalina developed four iterations using stippling, greyscale markers, graphite and pen.
concept: Before creating the renderings, Catalina developed a narrative describing how she imagined someone experiencing and using the space. The narrative then guided each rendering.
The project demonstrates material representation, texture, value, atmosphere, hand rendering and visual storytelling.

process.label: Idea
process.note: A narrative describing how someone experiences and uses the space.

process.label: Iteration
process.note: Four renderings: stippling, greyscale markers, graphite and pen.

process.label: Final
process.note: Four iterations of the same space.

title: Casa de Luz y Tierra
subtitle: Creative Dwelling
summary: A home designed around the routines and passions of a fictional client who paints, cooks and runs, with a day that starts early.
description: This project explored designing a home around the needs, routines and interests of a fictional client.
The program included a kitchen, primary bedroom, primary bathroom, studio, living room and dining space.
concept_title: A home for creativity and everyday life
concept: The fictional client has a passion for painting, cooking and running, and a routine that centers on early mornings.
Catalina's goal was to create a home that supports both creativity and everyday life through thoughtful and functional design.
The design went through multiple iterations and collaborative class feedback, which let Catalina refine layout, spatial relationships, functionality and responsiveness to the client.

process.label: Iteration

title: Hero Lair
subtitle: Project 1
summary: A home for Simba carved into the Moru Kopjes rock formation in the Serengeti, shaped by his identity, rituals and daily life.
description: This project explored the design of a lair for a chosen hero or villain based on their identity, rituals and daily life.
Catalina chose Simba from The Lion King and designed a home carved into the Moru Kopjes rock formation in the Serengeti.
concept: The spaces reflect Simba's connection to family, his connection to nature, and his leadership.
The architecture was designed to blend with its surrounding environment.

process.note: Simba's identity, rituals and daily life.

process.label: Design
process.note: A home carved into the Moru Kopjes, blending with its environment.

process.label: Final
process.note: Spaces that reflect family, nature and leadership.

quote.text: This research center is inspired by the complex system of pollination and the interconnected relationships that sustain the ecology of Philips Farm in Moscow, Idaho. The project explores how plants, pollinators, researchers, and visitors are all connected within the landscape, creating a space that celebrates nature through design while remaining sensitive and responsible to the local environment.

pitch: Architecture as a bridge between people and landscape. Inspired by the system of pollination, this field station supports two student researchers living and working at Philips Farm, with room for observation, study and collaboration, and a way for visitors to experience the site's ecology.

title: Olivier's Chocolate
subtitle: A Taste of Belgium, brought to Moscow, Idaho
summary: A collaborative urban renewal study near the Moscow silos, and one of its parcels: a chocolate shop with two homes, designed around a fictional Belgian chocolatier.
description: Legacy Crossing, Project 3 — Urban Renewal, was a collaborative project with the theme Arts, Beats & Eats. The class researched urban renewal, historical and contemporary precedents, existing redevelopment plans, the organizations involved and future development sites.

The class selected a site near the intersection of 6th and Jackson Street by the Moscow silos and divided it into seven parcels. Each student developed a potential business concept, and Catalina chose chocolatiering. The result is Olivier's Chocolate.
concept_title: A new home, a new community
concept: The concept follows a fictional Belgian chocolatier named Olivier, who moves to Moscow, Idaho to share his craft and build a new community.
The design draws from Belgian architecture, materials and craftsmanship, and explores identity, home, community and cultural connection.
The building includes a chocolate shop, two private living spaces with bedrooms, bathrooms and compact kitchens, and a shared washer/dryer.
